speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I will refer to this as the proposed transaction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I am therefore making a Ministerial Statement today to explain the Government's position and to set out the steps which it proposes to take.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I will start by setting out the circumstances in which Income, a former co-operative society or co-op, was corporatised in 2022, as that background has relevance to the proposed transaction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I will also explain the exemption from section 88 of the Co-operative Societies Act or CSA which Income had obtained in the course of its corporatisation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I will then set out our views on the proposed transaction and the next steps.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income has a unique history and has played a special role in serving Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The concept of Labour Movement co-ops, also known as social enterprises, was first conceived at NTUC's Modernisation Seminar in 1969, where Mr Devan Nair articulated the need for the Labour Movement to turn into a social institution to serve Singaporean workers in various ways.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Then, Dr Goh Keng Swee urged NTUC to set up social enterprises in areas such as life insurance and essential consumer goods to meet the needs of the working population.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income was subsequently established in 1970 under the name NTUC Income Insurance Co-operative Limited.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It was Singapore's first co-op under the aegis of the Labour Movement.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over the years, Income played an important role in providing affordable insurance for workers and Singaporeans at large.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: NE was set up in 2012 as a holding entity for the various social enterprises under the Labour Movement.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Since 2012, NE has strongly supported the growth of Income, progressively contributing to the share capital of Income.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This included $100 million of capital during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, which was critical for the continued viability of Income.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With NE's support, Income has grown through the years to serve Singaporeans' needs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income has also made progress in its social mission to provide accessible and inclusive insurance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, it launched the Complete Cancer Care to offer Singaporeans comprehensive support from cancer diagnosis to recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It has also launched a suite of products over the years to cater to the financial needs of specific underserved segments.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These include SpecialCare Autism and Down syndrome, Care4MigrantWorkers, and products that provide coverage for mental health conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2022, Income embarked on a corporatisation exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It wanted to change its legal form from a co-op to a company and to replicate the existing co-op shareholding profile in the shareholding profile of the new corporate entity to be set up.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income needed to evolve to meet tightening regulations for financial institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, the co-op structure has limitations and is not conducive to stronger capital access and good value strategic partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the face of increasing global competition, Income wanted a corporate structure which would put it on par with its competitors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income therefore proposed to convert itself into a corporate entity, with the members of the co-op receiving pari passu distribution in specie of shares in the new entity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income also sought an exemption from section 88 of the CSA – which applies when a Co-op is put in liquidation – because Income was not, in substance, being liquidated.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It was only changing its legal form and would continue to be engaged in the same business.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The exemption was therefore needed to facilitate the corporatisation exercise, so that Income's accumulated surplus, beyond par value, could be carried over to the new corporate entity to allow it to continue the business.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I will come back to this point later in my speech.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At that time, Income explained to its members, the public and to the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) that corporatisation would also empower Income to drive greater social and economic value in a sustainable manner.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY wanted to understand Income's position in greater detail and met with Income on several occasions to discuss the matter.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the course of our meetings, Income emphasised a few salient points to MCCY.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, the insurance landscape had fundamentally changed since 1970 and corporatisation was critical to allow Income to effectively compete with other insurers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income pointed out that the local insurance market had matured by 2022, unlike in earlier years, when a significant working class segment was still underserved.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, Income was facing increasing competition from large insurance players as well as new technology players in the market.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Its existing structure as a co-op lacked the flexibility of a corporate structure and did not give it access to distribution channels or the ability to scale, either locally or globally.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, there was growing pressure to inject capital into Income to build up its financial strength, in response to regulatory requirements and market competition.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income explained that corporatisation was critical for it to achieve operational flexibility.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It also wanted to have better access to capital to pursue strategic growth options, compete effectively in the market and do well in its business in the long run.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The third key point made by Income was that its social mission focus would not change.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income made clear to its members and to MCCY that the corporatisation exercise would only change its legal form from a co-op to a non-listed corporate entity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The new corporate entity would remain an NTUC social enterprise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In our discussions, Income assured MCCY, and I quote, that "post-corporatisation, Income will be able to grow more significantly in scale and deliver its social mandate as a significant player in the insurance industry".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income wanted more flexibility to establish partnerships that could build up its capital base so that it could sustain its social mission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In its letter to MCCY dated 27 June 2022, Income stated, and I quote: "We believe that, pursuant to the corporatisation, Co-Op", which is Income, in this case, "will be regarded to offer a more attractive proposition to investors and strategic partners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This would, in turn, allow Co-Op to raise capital more easily and thereby grow and unlock value for existing and new shareholders and policy-holders, and further its social mission through a sustainability agenda", unquote.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Registry for Co-operative Societies told Income that it had to address the public perception that NTUC social enterprises would be seen as moving away from co-op values.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In response, the CEO of Income confirmed that even after corporatisation, Income would not change its purpose and values.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At its extraordinary general meeting (EGM) in 2022, Income reiterated that the new company would continue operating as a social enterprise of NE and sustain its social mission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We agree that social enterprises need to do well in order to do good.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This includes having good financial and market discipline, in order for Income to be able to pursue its social mission more effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I said earlier that as part of the corporatisation exercise, Income had applied for a Ministerial exemption from section 88 of the CSA.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Under section 88 of the CSA, when a co-op decides to cease being a co-op and is wound up, its members can only be paid their original share capital plus any unpaid dividends up to a cap, after settling the costs of liquidation and the co-op's liabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Any surplus in the co-op beyond that will be transferred to the Co-operative Societies Liquidation Account, or the CSLA, to be applied for the benefit of the co-op sector generally.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is the framework under the CSA, when a co-op is wound up.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Technically, Income would be required to comply with section 88, as Income, the co-op, would be wound up after corporatisation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, as I explained, Income was not in fact ceasing its business.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It was proposing to convert from a co-op into a corporate entity for the reasons outlined above.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The corporatisation was to strengthen Income's capital base and financial adequacy in order for it to carry out its business better.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For these reasons, carrying over Income's surplus to the new corporate entity to support the business would be an integral part of the exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In announcing the proposed transaction, NE and Income had said that it was needed to strengthen Income so that it could continue with its social mission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They explained that insurance is a long-tail business.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income's capital buffers have repeatedly come under pressure over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: NE has supported Income with capital injections but cannot continue to do so on its own.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That is why Income has proposed this transaction with Allianz, to find a strong partner that can complement NE in strengthening Income, so that it can sustain its social mission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income, with Allianz and NE, had also committed to continue pursuing Income's social mission even after the transaction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In its announcement, Allianz had also said that it intended for Income to continue participating in national insurance programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It assured the public of a seamless transition for policy-holders and said that it would continue to honour the contractual terms and conditions of the existing polices underwritten by Income.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY had no prior knowledge of the proposed transaction prior to the public announcements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When we first saw the announcements, we accepted the intent of the transaction, which is to strengthen Income.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We saw that Income would be engaged in a strategic partnership with a major reputable player in the industry.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This would strengthen Income's capital base and allow it to have more access to capital.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is consistent with the representations that Income had made to MCCY at the point of corporatisation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As we have said before, for Income to do good, it must first do well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In a Facebook post on 4 August, I pointed out that co-ops, as social enterprises, must be financially sustainable in order to better serve their members in a fast-changing economic environment.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleague, Minister of State Alvin Tan, also spoke in Parliament in the August session.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He explained that MCCY appreciated the competitive landscape that Income was operating in and understood how the transaction with Allianz would help Income achieve longer term financial sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Subsequent to the August session of Parliament, MCCY continued to do due diligence and enquire further into the proposed transaction, including on the various public queries which had been raised.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the course of this review, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) provided MCCY with further details on the proposed transaction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This included information which Allianz, Income and NE had submitted to MAS in respect of initiatives to optimise the capital of Income post-transaction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: From our review of this additional information, we gathered the following.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The parties intended to implement a number of initiatives to optimise Income's insurance business after completion of the acquisition.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The plan was for Income to run its insurance business more efficiently, without the need to hold as much capital as it presently does.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As such, post-transaction, Allianz contemplates that Income could reduce its existing share capital and return this capital to shareholders.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: NE and Income focused on bringing in a strong shareholder and believed that, even with these initiatives, the proposed transaction with Allianz would allow it to continue with its social mission for years to come.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These projections were submitted to MAS at around the time that the proposed transaction was announced, in mid-July 2024.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At that time, MAS had reviewed the information based on prudential grounds, focusing on whether Allianz was a fit and proper institution, and Allianz's financial strength and track record, so that the interests of Income's policy-holders would be safeguarded with a strong substantial shareholder.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MAS considered the planned capital optimisation from a prudential point of view, in accordance with its regulatory mandate.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Based on the plans submitted, MAS did not have reason for concern as Income was projected to continue to meet regulatory capital requirements with a healthy margin even with the capital reduction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, after the 6 August Parliamentary Sitting, MAS saw that Income's planned capital optimisation could be relevant to MCCY's views on the proposed transaction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MAS then shared the information with MCCY, including the terms of the proposed transaction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We accept that from a narrow commercial or even prudential perspective, capital optimisation measures that free up capital to be returned to shareholders, are not uncommon practices.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, MCCY is not confident that the proposed transaction would not affect the ability of the co-op movement as a whole, or of Income itself, to carry out its social mission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, we find it difficult to reconcile the proposed substantial capital reduction, soon after the transaction is completed, with Income's representations to MCCY during the corporatisation exercise that it was aiming to build up capital resources and enhance its financial strength.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The proposed capital reduction runs counter to the premise on which the exemption was given.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY has not seen any arrangement within the present transaction to account for the estimated S$2 billion surplus that was carried over to the new corporate entity, due to the exemption.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There is no clarity on how this sum will be directed towards advancing Income's social mission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, MCCY is not satisfied that Income will be able to continue fulfilling its social mission after the proposed transaction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There are no clear binding provisions or structural protections in the deal to ensure that Income's social mission will be discharged.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is also not clear what Income might do after the capital extraction, for example, to adjust or trim its insurance portfolio, and what impact this could have on policy-holders.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: NE has stated that it intends to maintain Income's social mission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY accepts that NE is making this commitment in good faith.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But MCCY is not confident that NE's intentions, or the assurances Income gave earlier to MCCY, can be upheld.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We had known earlier that the proposed transaction would leave NE as the minority shareholder in the new entity, with a minority of board positions and no ability to nominate the Chairman of the new Income entity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I should, however, make clear that the Government understands and accepts the strategic purpose behind Income's corporatisation exercise and its subsequent decision to form a partnership with Allianz.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It was to strengthen Income and make it more financially sustainable in the longer term.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Government also does not have concerns over Allianz's standing or suitability to acquire a majority stake in Income.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As I noted earlier, MCCY supports Income's efforts to find a strong partner so as to strengthen its capital base and market position.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Allianz is a major global insurance company and asset manager that can bring financial strength and expertise to Income.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our concern is only over the terms and structure of this specific transaction, particularly in the context of the preceding corporatisation exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Income was a co-op, and subject to the objectives and obligations of being a co-op.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Therefore, we also have to take into account the circumstances in which Income was corporatised and obtained an exemption from section 88 of the CSA.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Hence, our assessment of the viability of this transaction must go beyond prudential considerations alone.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Income is now a corporate entity, it is no longer subject to the jurisdiction of the Registrar of Co-ops.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The approval or otherwise of the proposed transaction now rests with MAS under the Insurance Act.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Sections 26 and 27 of the Insurance Act require a person to seek the prior written approval of MAS to obtain effective control or become a substantial shareholder of a licensed insurer incorporated in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The proposed transaction therefore requires MAS' approval to proceed.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When MAS assesses an application under these sections, it considers a range of criteria on prudential grounds such as the financial strength and track record of the applicant, and whether it is fit and proper.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The amendments will be scoped specifically to only apply to a licensed insurer that is the subject of an application under sections 26 and 27 of the Insurance Act and, where the licensed insurer is a co-operative, has acquired the business of a co-operative, or has a substantial shareholder or effective controller which is a co-operative.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is based on the Government's recognition that insurance co-ops are a special category of insurers with a social mission for which the views of the Minister overseeing co-ops need to be considered.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Bill will therefore provide for the Minister-in-charge of MAS to consider the views of the Minister responsible for the administration of the CSA.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And for the Minister-in-charge of MAS to withhold approval to such applications if he considers that it is in the public interest to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I should add that MCCY may also consider future amendments to the CSA to give the Government stronger levers over co-ops that may wish to be corporatised.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At that time, I had replied that we were still looking into the issue.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Singh had asked whether NE had given its undertaking to hold on to its shares in Income, and I quote, "for an indefinite period", unquote, referring to views that Mr Tan Suee Chieh, a former CEO of Income and Group CEO of NE, had published.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our fact finding shows that Mr Tan did indeed state, when he was Group CEO of NE, at a meeting of the Income Board on 21 November 2014, that he, referring to Mr Tan, was, I quote, "confident that the NE Board would agree to a request to extend this undertaking not to redeem to an indefinite period, as NE was prepared to convert its shares to the new class of irredeemable shares once the legislation was passed", unquote.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, the letter that was eventually sent by NE to Income on 11 February 2015 stated, and I quote, "Our shareholding in NTUC Income is thus committed over the long term, and there is no intention of withdrawing the share capital to be subscribed".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In short, the answer is, there was no specific commitment that the shares would not be redeemed indefinitely; neither was there a commitment that the shares would not be transferred to someone else.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: More importantly, Sir, the commitment given by NE to Income in 2015 is no longer relevant in today's context.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Back in 2015, Income was a co-op whose members had the right to withdraw their share capital at any time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This was a problem because Income needed a stable capital base to support its insurance business, but its members' share capital, being redeemable at any time, could not be counted towards MAS' capital adequacy requirements for insurers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When Income subsequently corporatised, NE's shares in Income, the co-op, were converted into shares in the new company, which are also not withdrawable.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Therefore, there is no longer a need for any undertaking by NE not to redeem its shares because all the shares are now permanent.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Co-ops have been helping the community, providing affordable services, especially to the underserved for close to a century.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They reinforce our nation's social fabric, complementing the efforts of the public and private sectors, helping to create a caring and cohesive community in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We appreciate that co-ops have to balance the constant tension between doing good and doing well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On its part, the Government agrees that co-ops must do well before they can do good.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY has been and will continue supporting the co-op movement through various capability building efforts and enhancements to legislation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, MCCY is responsible to ensure that the co-ops continue to uphold their social missions to benefit Singaporeans and our wider society, as they seek to do well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is why we have seen it fit to intervene, in the proposed transaction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members can take time to study the Bill and take part in the debate on 16 October and raise clarifications on the Bill and related matters during that debate.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Clarifications may be asked arising from the Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some of our Choa Chu Kang residents are Income policy-holders and they have expressed concern, and are grateful to the Government that they have looked into this and deemed that the transaction in its current form is not in the public interest.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Minister mentioned just now that the Government intervened in this transaction but has not closed the doors to any potential other restructuring of the particular deal.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, my question is whether or not Income can find new partners or is it open to Allianz to restructure it and come back with future proposals?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The concern is because Allianz is a foreign company and it is not the basis that just because it is an offer from a foreign company that we are intervening.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My second question is on the Government's commitment to support co-operatives as social enterprises.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I cannot agree more that they need to do well in order to do good.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Quite apart from Income, are there any other co-ops in Singapore and how are their objectives supported?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And the Minister mentioned the Co-operative Societies Liquidation Account, the CSLA.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The first is on Allianz and whether or not we have foreclosed the possibility of a future transaction, whether with Allianz or any other partner.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: By all accounts, Allianz has put forward a credible, sound proposal and from a financial perspective it makes sense for Income to look at an entity that has global presence, strong networks and it is able to enter into it with a view towards a long-term strategic partnership.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, do not read into this as suggesting that we are not open to a foreign entity partnering with Income or indeed, whether it is Allianz or indeed, any other entity.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I hope that answers the first of the Member's questions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In relation to co-ops, they come under my Ministry.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are a variety of different co-ops and there are NTUC co-ops which helps look after the underserved workers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are also campus co-ops where, Members might remember, the National University of Singapore, Nanyang Technological University and Ngee Ann, they all run co-ops for the benefit of students.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are also co-ops which help the sectors of society which need special attention.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, Running Hour is a co-op that helps inclusivity in sports.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is also a co-op that looks after the employment of persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, these are the different types of co-ops that come under the framework.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We support the co-ops in a number of ways, through enhancing the work that they do, supporting them through changes in the CSA that helps them in their business, that allows them to evolve and keep up with the times, and also has a fund that I mentioned, the CSLA, which MCCY and the Registrar manages and administers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This fund, from time to time, helps co-ops with training of personnel and showing that they are the best people running each of the co-ops, and on occasion also sets up a fund like we have done recently, just earlier this year, on the Empowering Communities Fund, which helps to look after a specific segment of society, that is funded from the CSLA.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, this is one reason we maintain the CSLA, to look at how we can benefit co-ops as a whole in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: MAS knew about the capital extraction plan by around mid-July.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, what was MAS' assessment of this plan?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Third, why did MAS not share more information about the capital extraction with MCCY earlier?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister Chee Hong Tat, do you want to respond?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: At that time, MAS had reviewed the high-level submitted information based on prudential grounds, focusing on whether Allianz was fit and proper, looking at its financial strength and track record, and looking at the interests of Income's policy-holders and ensuring that this will be safeguarded with a new, strong, substantial shareholder.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, those were the elements of what MAS was looking at when they received this plan and they received the proposal from Allianz.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is when MAS then decided that there were grounds to share the information with MCCY and that it was appropriate for MAS to do so – and that was what happened.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I hope that clarifies the questions that Ms Pereira asked.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister Edwin Tong, would you like to add to that?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: My question to the MCCY Minister is, Income is now no longer a co-op, it is a corporate now.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Hence, my query is how would MCCY still be able to exercise its oversight, whether it is for these transactions on the grounds of public interest or to hold Income to fulfilling its social mission that it has committed to, going forward?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Income today is no longer a co-op and I have explained in my speech why it had taken steps to become a corporate entity.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And because it is now a corporate entity, we must allow Income to operate like a company with autonomy in how it pursues business decisions, how it makes its plans and its financial arrangements and so on, as a corporate vehicle.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But a corporate vehicle can also be a social enterprise within this framework.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, if you ask how this could be done, for example, ring-fencing some of the products which I mentioned earlier, which serves a segment of society, ring-fencing this to ensure that whatever business you conduct, you will always be in a particular segment of looking after this underserved segment of society at a lower cost.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If this arrangement was not being proposed, Income was free to use this surplus as it has been doing, to carry out the social mission, it would embark on business obviously and it must meet the usual capital adequacy requirements and so on, but it would be able to exercise some discretion over this surplus.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But moving forward, which I think is the thrust of your broad point, there are a number of ways in which a corporate can still remain a social enterprise in the way in which it conducts its business.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Was the Government and MCCY already aware in July that despite assurances given by NTUC and Allianz that there are no existing safeguards which precluded Allianz from optimising the capital base of NTUC Income, which, as I understand correctly from Minister's Statement just now, is one of the key reasons that it now steps in.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: As such, can I ask Minister to clarify upon reflection if NTUC Income should have been allowed to be a corporate and be given an exemption from compliance with section 88 of the Co-operative Societies Act?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is the requirement under the Insurance Act and by MAS.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the current co-operative, or at that time, current co-operative structure, was not conducive to it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, it made investments or strategic partnerships with a co-op less attractive.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There were some restrictions on how much dividend could be declared, out of which year's profits and there was also a limit to it and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These limitations do not apply to a corporate entity.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so, these amongst others, were the reasons why we supported Income when they approached us and discussed their plans with us.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It applies in all other cases – the fund with the surplus after you pay off liabilities would be put into the CSLA.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But as I had explained, this was not a scenario where Income was going to be liquidated, wound up and cease its business.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, it was carrying on the same business, with the assurance that it would see to its social mission, in a sense, in a new skin, in a corporate vehicle set-up, but continuing with the same business, fundamentally.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so, in that respect, taken as a whole, the exemptions were considered to be suitable and granted, so that Income can carry on and will be able to take advantage of the capital surpluses in its new vehicle.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will explore all of this when we look at the CSA in detail.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Given that the need for more capital was the basis to justify the corporatisation of Income and then again, subsequently, to justify the sale of Income to Allianz which is in direct contradiction with the plan to reduce capital, will any action be taken against those responsible for misleading the public and the Government?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I am not sure Ms Poa heard my Statement or understood it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The deal, on its own, was priced appropriately; the terms were put up.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And as I had mentioned, even after the capital extraction, the financial viability, the capital adequacy requirements and ratios will be satisfied.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That was the framework in which this was proceeded with.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And NE and Income, as I also explained, believed in good faith that this strategic partnership would strengthen Income as an entity to allow it to compete in the insurance business with the benefit of a partner like Allianz.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have a different view of that for reasons which are not associated with the financial viability or sustainability of the proposal.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, there is no misleading as far as this is concerned.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But we believe that if you were to look at the representations that were given in the context of the corporatisation and the exemption exercise, we think that this goes counter to that arrangement and we have a different opinion from NE and Income as to its ability to still continue to carry out its social mission.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And as I said, cumulatively with other factors which we have also seen, such as the lack of structures in the agreement to protect the social mission or to advance it, and also coupled with the fact that it would no longer have majority control at the shareholding and also at the board level.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But there is no question that there has been any misleading.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have just taken a view of them differently from NE and Income as to its ability to carry out its social mission thereafter.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is a question for Minister Chee Hong Tat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The strategic intent for this deal is to help policy-makers in the longer run.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: So, in MAS' review of this deal and that now that this deal will be halted, what does it mean for policy-holders in the short to the long run?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Will the terms of their policy to their board be safeguarded and should policy-holders be concerned?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I mentioned this in the August Sitting in response to Ms He Ting Ru that the deal is still subject to MAS regulatory approval.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this is not something that MAS has approved.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Minister Edwin Tong has explained why the Government has decided to make amendments to the Insurance Act to give the Minister-in-charge of MAS the powers to consider the views and concerns of the Minister for MCCY on public interest grounds.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The best way to protect policy-holders in addition to ensuring that the licensees have sufficient capital to meet the necessary capital adequacy ratios is also to ensure that we have a competitive insurance industry.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because then, that will give choice and options to policy-holders to be able to choose what is the best product, the most competitive product, that can meet their needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But nevertheless, as a globally oriented player, Allianz would presumably have done some of its regulatory risk assessment and homework prior to the actual announcement on 17 June.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And based on Minister Tong's statement, it seems that it was MCCY that was ultimately caught unaware.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And I understand that the proposed urgent Bill scheduled for Wednesday is meant to, in part, remediate this lapse in intra-government communication.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Nevertheless, I wonder what this means for the reputation of MAS as a reliable channel for Government sentiment for potential future deals that would require regulatory approval.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: What of other deals where different agencies or Ministries other than MCCY may have relevant input?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I appreciate why Assoc Prof Lim asked this question because it is also something that is important to us.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First of all, I really, from my heart, welcome the Government's decision to block this transaction, which I have questioned very much at the 6 August Sitting, with the help of information from many well-informed Singaporeans, like Mr Tan Suee Chieh.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is a big relief to NTUC policy-holders, of which I am one.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Minister today, in announcing the turnaround of the Government's position, because what we heard on 6 August is actually very different.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, from what the Minister has said, it seems that all the processes are proper.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, it begs the question, my first question is, who in the Government, in such big financial transaction, will be the final goalkeeper?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Who is the one who will finally look at the outcome of the deal or any policy decisions, and not just the processes?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It seems that NE has gone through the right process, MAS has also done the first round of assessment and the case was presented to Parliament on 6 August.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We were debating, we were asking questions in a different direction.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We are trying to say at that Sitting that this transaction needs to be reconsidered.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But of course, the Minister and the Minister of State at that time had given us very different impressions.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, my first question is, in the future, when we have big financial transactions like this, can we get the assurance from the Government that there will be someone – in this case, we are happy that MCCY acted as a goalkeeper to look at the outcome of this transaction.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, in the future, can I get assurance who is going to do this goalkeeper role?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second question I have is, what Minister Chee had mentioned just now, is that part of MAS' responsibility is to assess the deal in the interest of policy-holders.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the deal involves the acquirer extracting capital from the entity, can this fit into the criterion that it will be in the interest of the policy-holders?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If it does not, then, is it that MAS had not done its job?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: If I am not mistaken, one is directed at Minister Tong and the other directed at Minister Chee.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I have explained earlier in my reply to Ms Pereira that MAS will look at the proposal from a prudential point of view.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is MAS' role as the prudential regulator for the insurance industry.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, when the MAS team looks at that, they at that point in time, were not privy to the details of the exemption, of MCCY's exemption from section 88.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I had explained that earlier in my reply to Ms Pereira.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, from the MAS team's point of view, this is a proposal, they were assessing it from a prudential point of view and they looked at after the proposed capital reduction, would Income still be able to meet its necessary capital adequacy ratio?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And if so, then from a prudential point of view, there is no reason for the regulator to object.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And this goes back to the point that Assoc Prof Jamus Lim raised earlier.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we want to be a regulator of good standing internationally, we have got to operate in a rules-based system, looking at what our requirements are as regulator and apply them consistently and in an even-handed manner.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And then, by working together, MAS, MCCY, in a whole-of-Government manner, and this is how we will work as a Government, we will work across different Ministries, across different departments for the benefit of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Yes, initially, there was an information gap, as I explained.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But once we shared the information, we work closely together, we work in a coordinated manner, and this is why we are bringing this Bill to Parliament for consideration.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Leong made a reference to the Sitting in August and also some public views on the transaction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I was not here in August, but I have since read the transcripts and understand what the Member had said.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There were a number of views that were put out like, this transaction should not go on because the shares were supposed to be not redeemable or that it cannot be sold.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I think the Member heard me explain earlier the background to why and how I answered the Leader of Opposition's query.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the point really is that it is in the interest of Income in 2022 to have corporatised, I explained that, and for it to use this corporate vehicle to look at possibilities for partnerships, which it has now done and they found Allianz in this case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I said, the objection is not to Allianz as an entity or to the financial suitability of its plans per se, but rather the questions that we have decided which followed after we reviewed the information, as the Member heard Minister Chee say earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I would add to that by saying that is exactly how, when the Member mentioned the goalkeeper, this works.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: MAS would not share all and sundry information.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Member cannot expect that every time information about a potential application, an acquisition or a deal is proposed, is made, and information given to MAS that it is shared with all and sundry.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, in this case, after they realised that there are various issues which MCCY might be concerned about, they then shared the relevant information with us.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is how we would work, to answer your point about having a goalkeeper.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I think I heard Minister Tong say earlier that MCCY was concerned that there were no structural protections in the deal to ensure that Income could continue its social mission.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: But the fact that Allianz would have a majority stake in Income Insurance under the proposed deal was known at least since 17 July 2024, when Income first made its public announcement.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Was this not a concern to MCCY in August?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Be that as it may, what structural protections does MCCY expect to be put in place in order for any sale of a co-op or social enterprise to proceed?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: For example, will it be the case that co-ops or social enterprises will not be allowed to sell a majority stake in their shares to an entity that does not have an explicit social mission?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I hope the Member has taken that into consideration and into account.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And what we knew after 6 August allowed us to look at it cumulatively.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On its own, as I mentioned my speech, losing board majority, losing shareholder majority were not itself factors which allowed us to reach a view that it was not in the public's interest.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the Member would appreciate that it is a balancing consideration.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the one hand, there is a strategic interest in wanting the partnership to strengthen Income, to ensure that it will remain competitive.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I hope that explains the sequence of events and that Mr Giam does not see the shadows which do not exist in this case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is about what we knew on 6 August and what we said, and even if the Member looked at the Hansard transcripts, what we said on 6 August was in relation to overarching purpose as strategic intent of Income looking for a partner, not so much that we knew the terms of this and we were talking about the terms of this on 6 August.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I hope that makes that clear for Mr Giam.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As to what would work, I had ventured that in my answer to Mr Liang earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, you might ringfence products using proceeds or surplus from the co-operative, as one example.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Or you might have terms contractually even without majority shareholding, which oblige the parties to operate in a particular way to fulfil social missions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, these are some examples of what they might be.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But as to what exactly such a deal should look like, I think that would be speculative and I would not go into that.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If the parties decide, at some juncture, that they want to reconsider this proposal and resubmit a proposal, we will consider it afresh at that point in time.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: That is Mr Leong, Ms He and Mr Liang Eng Hwa.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Are there any more hands besides these Members?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Okay, then Ms He Ting Ru, then Mr Leong and then Mr Liang.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I believe some of the concerns raised in Parliament in August were about financial sustainability and capital structure of the business going forward.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, I struggle to understand how withdrawing capital in the future can strengthen any entity's capital structure.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Given that there is public interest and social mission involved here, I think it is important that these reasons are articulated properly to help the public understand why there was this structure put in place, and I think it is also relevant because NE is still after all going to be a shareholder, albeit a minority one going forward, under the original proposed structure.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The short point is this: that a withdrawal must be seen in the context of several other factors and there was a plan.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the plan is to optimise capital and not so much just to withdraw per se.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, when you optimise capital, you can do it in a number of ways.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the context of an insurance company, maybe redeploy reinsurance, for example, to remove some of the risks and therefore you need to maintain less capital to deal with buffers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, these are factors that they take into account in looking at this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I take the point that these are discussions that obviously ought to be had with NE, moving forward, as to which types of proposals that maintain and allow us to fulfil the social mission can be countenanced.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That was what they put forth to MAS since the middle of July, but MAS has not approved the proposed capital reduction plan.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In fact, Ms He may recall, when I responded to her on 6 August during the Sitting, I used the Chinese phrase to describe the situation that the deal still required MAS' regulatory approval.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this deal is not approved yet and it is something that is still subject to MAS' regulatory approval, including the capital reduction plan.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Deputy Speaker, I have two questions, maybe for Minister Chee Hong Tat.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: One is, can the Minister confirm that in assessing the prudential requirements of the deal, MAS had taken into consideration the capital extraction, although the Minister said just now that MAS had not approved the capacity extraction?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Have they considered, even with the capital extraction, the prudential requirements are still satisfied?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The second question is maybe both Ministers can decide who to answer this question.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: For the last few months, we are of the impression that the information given is all that we have.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: This is a very important condition of any financial deal.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am surprised, I am shocked and I am very unhappy today that this important condition is not being disclosed to the Singaporeans, when we were all discussing about this deal.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, whose responsibility is it for not disclosing this information?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Can the Government give a commitment that it will pursue responsibility with regard to this?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Maybe the company and all that, because this is a very important condition for the financial deal.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is not something that MAS has approved because, as I mentioned repeatedly, the deal is still subject to MAS' regulatory approval.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, would MAS consider this proposed capital reduction in its overall assessment?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Leong always remind us that he has more than 30 years of experience in the financial sector.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I am sure Mr Leong would agree with me that as a regulator, it is only right that we assess the full proposal, including this element within the proposal.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Whether we agree with it or not, we have not yet come to a decision because this deal is still not yet approved by MAS.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But that is what the proposal put forth.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I hope that clarifies the first question that Mr Leong raised.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The second question – and I think my colleague Minister Tong may add on later – let me just say in response to Mr Leong that that is why we are coming to Parliament.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In Minister Tong's speech, he has explained clearly and in an open manner our key considerations, what are our concerns, including the proposal to reduce the capital in Income and why that is a concern to MCCY, bearing in mind the section 88 exemption that was earlier given and the undertaking and commitments that were given to MCCY.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I hope Mr Leong understands that this is not about withholding information.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is about coming to Parliament after we have put together the full picture, working across the whole-of-Government, between MAS, MCCY and also other agencies, to see what is the overall assessment of how we want to move forward on this important issue and then coming back to Parliament to present the information in an open manner and to propose that we amend the Insurance Act to give the Minister-in-charge of MAS the powers to consider the concerns and the views of the Minister for MCCY on public interest grounds.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is important for us to recognise that this deal is not yet approved and this deal is something that is ongoing, under consideration by shareholders, and that is why we have some urgency.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is why we are coming to Parliament to seek approval urgently.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister Edwin Tong, would you like to add to that?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I explained it in some detail in my speech and I hope that the Member will not mischaracterise it by suggesting that information has been withheld.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We explained why we believed that it is important for Income to have the ability to find and make arrangements for a partnership.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But as the Member knows, the transaction had not been approved.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We then got information from MAS, we shared the information and, as you heard me say earlier, this is how the Government works.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We studied the information carefully, went through, understood the transaction and its impact, understood it from a financial perspective, understood it from a social mission perspective.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Then, after coming to a view that it would not be in the public interest for this to proceed, we had to decide what is the best way to deal with this, to handle this, having regard to the fact that the Insurance Act gives MAS the ability to look at transactions from a financial or prudential perspective, but not from this angle, which is the views of the MCCY Minister overseeing co-operatives.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we had to reach a view as to not just that it is not in the public interest to proceed, but what we would do about it, which I am sure Mr Leong appreciates, is equally important.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is, after all, a live transaction, it is going on and there is market-sensitive information as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, the first available opportunity, we have come to Parliament, explained it in a Ministerial Statement, the background as well as the steps moving forward and then tabling a Bill, which we will put in in a few moments, for a debate on Wednesday, as much time as possible in the context given to Members, given that this is a live transaction and we cannot leave this state of uncertainty pending.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I hope Mr Leong appreciates that that is the scenario that we are in and that there is no question of any information being withheld, either from Parliament or from Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I will allow one last clarification from Mr Leong.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: You will have the opportunity to debate the merit and principles of the Bill at the Second Reading and Third Reading on Wednesday.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: So, could you make it a short clarification, please?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I would just like to say that I appreciate all the clarifications that both Ministers have done today.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: When I talk about responsibility, I am actually talking more about when Income made the announcement, were they withholding information?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Because we Singaporeans are all debating this deal.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: If this capital extraction is included right from the beginning in the deal, this information should have been made available to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Do either of the Ministers want to respond or we can leave it for the debate?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will have a further discussion on Wednesday when we do the Second Reading and the Third Reading.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But I want to say this – because I think it is important that we do not leave with the wrong impression – that for NTUC and NE, their objective of wanting to go into this deal was, indeed, to do what is right; and it is, indeed, to allow Income to be strong and to be able to do well so that it can continue to do good.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister Edwin Tong, would you like to add to that?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would just like to say that Mr Leong has been working for longer than I have been, in the financial sector.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: You know that this is an arrangement, this is a deal, and the parties submit proposals or plans to MAS, socialise them with MAS.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Member cannot expect this to be then made public to everyone.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Income has obligations to its shareholders as well, and this is a step that happens after the transaction is completed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They have not even applied to approve the transaction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, Mr Leong, be circumspect about making allegations that parties, whether the Government or Income, could be more open or are withholding information, because there is a due process as to how this is done.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: You do not go out there and produce information about a proposal when the transaction has not even been approved.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I hope Mr Leong sees it in that perspective.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: There being no other final clarifications, Mr Liang Eng Hwa.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is why we need to come to Parliament with the proposed Bill to give the Minister-in-charge of MAS the powers to be able to consider the views and the concerns of the Minister for MCCY on public interest grounds.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry, for the Insurance (Amendment) Bill.
